So that the sense is: they will beg of God thy countenance, so as to belong to the flock of believers; for outside the Church there is salvation for no one, just as outside the ark of Noe no one was saved from the flood[[Gen 7:23||]].

paras.t: Omnis gloria ejus, utpote filiæ regis, quæ nunc regina vocata est, et sponsa Christi atque Ecclesia, ab intus: id est, tota perfectio fidelium in interiori mentis decore consistit, non in exterioribus rebus caducis ac vanis. Deus enim intuetur cor, et mentem scrutatur; homo autem ea quæ foris sunt aspicit. Sed quia virtus interior procedere debet in exteriores sanctas operationes, quemadmodum Christus ait, Quid vocatis me, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico? ideo addit, in fimbriis aureis, circumamicta varietatibus: id est, gloria seu vitæ excellentia etiam consistit in operibus caritatis; et gloria seu perfectio ista circumamicta est varietatibus, id est actibus diversarum virtutum ornata: quia, ut ait Apostolus, caritas patiens est, benigna est, non æmulatur, non agit perperam, non inflatur, non quærit quæ sua sunt. Perfectio ergo christianorum animorum, in interioribus maxime sita est. Propter quod monet Apostolus: Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ, et induite novum hominem, qui secundum Deum creatus est. Et iterum exhortatur: Mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei.
paras.en: [[44:14|All the glory|Omnis gloria ejus]], namely [[44:14|of the king's daughter|filiæ regis]], who is now called queen, and the spouse of Christ, and the Church, [[44:14|is within|ab intus]]: that is, the whole perfection of the faithful consists in the inner beauty of the mind, not in outward things, which are perishable and vain. For God beholds the heart and searches the mind, while man looks on the things that are without[[1 Kings 16:7||]]. But since inner virtue must go forth into holy outward works (as Christ says: [[Luke 6:46|why call you me, Lord, Lord; and do not the things which I say|Quid vocatis me, Domine, Domine, et non facitis quæ dico]]?), he therefore adds: [[44:14|in golden borders|in fimbriis aureis]], [[44:15|Clothed round about with varieties|circumamicta varietatibus]]: that is, glory, or excellence of life, consists also in works of charity; and this glory or perfection is clothed round about with varieties, that is, adorned with the acts of diverse virtues; for, as the Apostle says, [[1 Cor 13:4|Charity is patient, is kind|caritas patiens est, benigna est]]: [[1 Cor 13:4|envieth not, dealeth not perversely, is not puffed up|non æmulatur, non agit perperam, non inflatur]], [[1 Cor 13:5|seeketh not her own|non quærit quæ sua sunt]]. The perfection of Christian souls, then, lies chiefly in what is within. For which reason the Apostle warns: [[Eph 4:23|be renewed in spirit of your mind|Renovamini spiritu mentis vestræ]], [[Eph 4:24|And put on the new man, who according to God is created|et induite novum hominem, qui secundum Deum creatus est]]. And again he exhorts: [[2 Cor 7:1|let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God|Mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis et spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in timore Dei]].

paras.t: Adducentur regi virgines post eam: id est, post primitivam Christi Ecclesiam adducentur ad Christum per prædicatores sanctos, homines mente et corpore continentes et integri; proximæ ejus, id est conjugati ac ceteri qui virginibus appropinquant, quoad hoc quod voluptatibus carnis non adhærent finaliter, afferentur tibi, o Christe, per fidem et cultum devotum. In ipsa enim Ecclesia congregantur virgines et conjugati; et omnes Christo uniuntur per fidem et gratiam. De his namque virginibus Christus in Evangelio dicit: Sunt eunuchi qui se castraverunt propter regnum Dei. De quibus scriptum est: Non dicat eunuchus, Ego lignum aridum: quia hæc dicit Dominus eunuchis, Qui custodierint fœdus meum, et elegerint quæ volui, dabo eis in domo mea et muris meis locum et nomen melius a filiis ac filiabus.
paras.en: [[44:15|After her shall virgins be brought to the king|Adducentur regi virgines post eam]]: that is, after the primitive Church of Christ, men continent and whole in mind and body shall be brought to Christ by holy preachers; [[44:15|her neighbours|proximæ ejus]], that is, the married and the others who come near to the virgins in this, that they do not cleave to the pleasures of the flesh as their end, [[44:15|shall be brought to thee|afferentur tibi]], O Christ, through faith and devout worship. For in the Church herself virgins and married people are gathered together, and all are united to Christ by faith and grace. Of these virgins Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 19:12|there are eunuchs, who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven|Sunt eunuchi qui se castraverunt propter regnum Dei]]. Of them it is written: [[Is 56:3|let not the eunuch say|Non dicat eunuchus]]: [[Is 56:3|I am a dry tree|Ego lignum aridum]]; [[Is 56:4|For thus saith the Lord to the eunuchs|quia hæc dicit Dominus eunuchis]]: [[Is 56:4|They that shall keep|Qui custodierint]] [[Is 56:4|my covenant|fœdus meum]], [[Is 56:4|and shall choose the things that please me|et elegerint quæ volui]], [[Is 56:5|I will give to them in my house, and within my walls, a place, and a name better than sons and daughters|dabo eis in domo mea et muris meis locum et nomen melius a filiis ac filiabus]].

paras.t: Afferentur in lætitia et exsultatione, id est, cum gaudio mentis et corporis ad Christum accedent, et ei deservient; adducentur in templum regis, id est in triumphantem Ecclesiam seu regnum cœlorum post hujus exilii incolatum.
paras.en: [[44:16|They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing|Afferentur in lætitia et exsultatione]], that is, they shall come to Christ with joy of mind and body, and shall serve him devotedly; [[44:16|they shall be brought into the temple of the king|adducentur in templum regis]], that is, into the Church triumphant, or the kingdom of heaven, after their sojourn in this exile.

paras.t: Pro patribus tuis nati sunt tibi filii: id est, loco Patriarcharum et Prophetarum orti sunt tibi, o Ecclesia Dei, Apostoli atque discipuli Christi, qui patribus successerunt, et ex eorum semine nati sunt; constitues eos, o Christe, principes super omnem terram: nam in illis terris, quas sancti Apostoli ad fidem converterunt, principatum sortiti sunt, sicut Joannes in Asia, Andreas in Achaia, Petrus et Paulus in Italia, Thomas et Bartholomæus in India. De hac enim missione et principatu Apostolorum ait Christus per Isaiam: Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam, in Lydiam, tenentes sagittam; in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe, ad eos qui non audierunt de me; et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus.
paras.en: [[44:17|Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee|Pro patribus tuis nati sunt tibi filii]]: that is, in the place of the Patriarchs and Prophets there have arisen for thee, O Church of God, the Apostles and disciples of Christ, who succeeded the fathers and were born of their seed; [[44:17|thou shalt make them|constitues eos]], O Christ, [[44:17|princes over all the earth|principes super omnem terram]]: for in those lands which the holy Apostles converted to the faith they obtained the princedom, as John in Asia, Andrew in Achaia, Peter and Paul in Italy, Thomas and Bartholomew in India. For of this mission and princedom of the Apostles Christ says through Isaias: [[Is 66:19|I will send of them that shall be saved, to the Gentiles into the sea, into Africa, and Lydia them that draw the bow: into Italy, and Greece, to the islands afar off, to them that have not heard of me|Mittam ex eis qui salvati fuerint, ad gentes in mare, in Africam, in Lydiam, tenentes sagittam; in Italiam et Græciam, ad insulas longe, ad eos qui non audierunt de me]]; [[Is 66:19|And they shall declare my glory to the Gentiles|et annuntiabunt gloriam meam gentibus]].

paras.t: Memor ero ego Propheta, auctor psalmi istius, vel ego Ecclesia, nominis tui, Domine rex Christe, in omni generatione et generationem. Quamdiu enim psalmus iste a fidelibus legitur, tamdiu Propheta Domini recordatur, quia alios ad Dei recordationem inducit. Ecclesia quoque indesinenter nomen Christi prædicando annuntiat. Propterea populi christiani confitebuntur tibi, id est, laudabunt te, atque ad honorem nominis tui peccata sua aperient, in æternum, id est usque ad finem mundi, quamdiu fides christiana duraverit, et in sæculum sæculi: id est, laus ista in præsenti vita incipitur, et in futuro sæculo sine fine continuabitur.
paras.en: I will [[44:18|remember|Memor ero]] [Denis reads *Memor ero*, "I will remember", where the Vulgate has *Memores erunt*, "they shall remember"], I the Prophet, the author of this psalm, or I the Church, [[44:18|thy name|nominis tui]], O Lord, Christ the King, [[44:18|throughout all generations|in omni generatione et generationem]]. For as long as this psalm is read by the faithful, so long does the Prophet remember the Lord, since he leads others to the remembrance of God. The Church too unceasingly proclaims the name of Christ by preaching it. [[44:18|Therefore shall people|Propterea populi]], Christian peoples, [[44:18|praise thee|confitebuntur tibi]] [*confitebuntur* means both "shall praise" and "shall confess"], that is, shall praise thee, and to the honour of thy name shall lay open their sins, [[44:18|for ever|in æternum]], that is, to the end of the world, as long as the Christian faith shall last, [[44:18|yea, for ever and ever|et in sæculum sæculi]]: that is, this praise is begun in the present life and will be continued without end in the world to come.

paras.t: Postremo pensandum, quod triplex est Christi sponsa, videlicet: universalis, quæ est Ecclesia; particularis, scilicet anima fidelis; et singularis, utpote Virgo divina. Quemadmodum ergo Cantica canticorum de hac triplici Christi sponsa exponi possunt, ita quæ nunc dicta sunt de sponsa Christi universali, exponi possunt de sponsa ejus particulari ac singulari.
paras.en: Lastly, it should be weighed that the spouse of Christ is threefold: universal, which is the Church; particular, namely the faithful soul; and singular, that is, the divine Virgin. As, then, the Canticle of Canticles can be expounded of this threefold spouse of Christ, so what has now been said of Christ's universal spouse can be expounded of his particular and of his singular spouse.

paras.t: Quælibet namque anima pia atque fidelis, Christo per fidem unita, per caritatem desponsata, atque a Christo bonis operibus fecundata, dici potest regina, tanquam summi regis filia, Christi coheres ac sponsa, a Spiritu Sancto lumine gratiæ imprægnata. Et ista regina adstat a dextris Christi in vestitu deaurato, secundum intellectum expositum. Cetera quoque faciliter applicari possunt ad quamlibet animam sanctam.
paras.en: For any devout and faithful soul, united to Christ by faith, espoused to him by charity and made fruitful by Christ in good works, can be called a queen, as the daughter of the highest king, co-heir and spouse of Christ, made to conceive by the Holy Ghost with the light of grace. And this queen stands at the right hand of Christ [[44:10|in gilded clothing|in vestitu deaurato]], in the sense expounded above. The rest too can easily be applied to any holy soul.

paras.t: Propriissime autem conveniunt ista Virgini benedictæ. Ipsa est enim unica illa ac summa Regina adstans semper a dextris Filii sui: quæ ineffabiliter delectat Patrem æternum, et placet incomparabiliter Sponso ac Filio suo, quemadmodum ait ad eam Sponsus cœlestis: Pulchra es, amica mea, suavis et decora; et iterum, Una est columba mea, perfecta mea. Adstat vero Regina hæc Regi gloriæ in vestitu deauratissimo, splendidissimo, ac rubicundissimo: quoniam ipsa caritate Dei et proximi ineffabiliter atque excellentissime æstuabat, et æstuat, ardentissimo optans affectu Christi Filii sui mortem et sanguinem fructificare in nobis, eratque sanctis operibus penitus superplena. Propter quod ipsa in Canticis proclamat: Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo. Unde de ea in Proverbiis habetur: Fortitudo et decor indumentum ejus. Erat etiam circumdata varietate universarum virtutum, sicut de ea Salomon est locutus: Inæstimabilis odor in vestimentis ejus, id est mira fragrantia spiritualis dulcedinis in virtutibus atque operibus suis. Nam et de tali odore Paulus testatur: Christi bonus odor sumus in omni loco. Et Moyses dicit: Odoratus est Dominus odorem suavitatis, id est piæ devotionis.
paras.en: But these things fit the blessed Virgin most properly of all. For she is that one and highest Queen who stands ever at the right hand of her Son; who ineffably delights the eternal Father and pleases her Spouse and Son beyond compare, as the heavenly Spouse says to her: [[Cant 6:3|Thou art beautiful, O my love, sweet and comely|Pulchra es, amica mea, suavis et decora]]; and again: [[Cant 6:8|One is my dove, my perfect one|Una est columba mea, perfecta mea]]. And this Queen stands by the King of glory in clothing most golden, most splendid and most ruddy; for she burned, and burns, ineffably and most excellently with charity towards God and her neighbour, desiring with most ardent affection that the death and blood of Christ her Son should bear fruit in us; and she was filled to overflowing with holy works. For which reason she cries out in the Canticle: [[Cant 2:5|Stay me up with flowers, compass me about with apples: because I languish with love|Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo]]. Hence it is said of her in Proverbs: [[Prov 31:25|Strength and beauty are her clothing|Fortitudo et decor indumentum ejus]]. She was also [[44:10|surrounded with variety|circumdata varietate]] of all the virtues, as Solomon spoke of her: Priceless is the fragrance in her garments[[Cant 4:11||]] [the margin has "cf. Cant. iv, 11", where the Spouse says "the smell of thy garments, as the smell of frankincense"; Denis's words are not those of the Vulgate], that is, a wonderful fragrance of spiritual sweetness in her virtues and works. For Paul too testifies of such a fragrance: [[2 Cor 2:15|we are the good odour of Christ|Christi bonus odor sumus]] in every place. And Moses says: [[Gen 8:21|the Lord smelled a sweet savour|Odoratus est Dominus odorem suavitatis]], that is, of devout piety.

paras.t: Denique huic Filiæ dicitur: Audi, filia, quæcumque in lege et Prophetis conscripta sunt, et quæ loquitur in te Dominus Deus; audi etiam salutationem angelicam; et vide, quæ, quanta et qualia Deus promisit hominibus per Prophetas; et inclina aurem tuam, ut divinæ inspirationi in omnibus acquiescas, atque angelicæ annuntiationi credas, assensumque præbeas; et obliviscere populum tuum, id est Israelem secundum carnem et litteram, non secundum spiritum et spiritualem interpretationem, et domum patris tui, a quo carnaliter genita es, quatenus patri spirituum in cunctis adhæreas. Tunc enim concupiscet rex Messias Unigenitus Dei decorem tuum interiorem, scilicet humilitatem, castitatem, caritatem. Concupivit enim tam vehementer Filius Dei decorem Mariæ, ut exsultaret quasi gigas ad currendam viam, descenderetque in uterum ejus purissimum atque dulcissimum, assumens sibi ex ea corpus humanum, ac partem virginalis substantiæ suæ divinitati uniret. Hinc namque in Canticis ait ad eam: Ostende mihi faciem tuam; sonet vox tua in auribus meis. Vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora. O quantum dilexit te Deus, Virgo dignissima! Quam beatissima es, Domina mea, quæ Deum verum concipere, nutrire, parere, contrectare, lactare, osculari, amplecti, et ad incrementa usque perducere meruisti! Bene dicere poteras illud Salomonis, Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus; illud quoque, Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur. Nam utique frequenter adolescentulus ille candidissimus puer Jesus tecum in lectulo florido conquievit, dormivit, et ubera tua virginea suxit, te blande adspiciens, dulciter osculans, reverentissimeque complectens.
paras.en: Lastly, it is said to this Daughter: [[44:11|Hearken, O daughter|Audi, filia]], to all that is written in the law and the Prophets, and to what the Lord God speaks in thee; hearken also to the angel's greeting[[Luke 1:28||]] [the margin gives Luke i, 28–33]; [[44:11|and see|et vide]] what things, how great and of what kind, God promised to men through the Prophets; [[44:11|and incline thy ear|et inclina aurem tuam]], so as to yield to the divine inspiration in all things, and to believe the angel's message and give it thy assent; [[44:11|and forget thy people|et obliviscere populum tuum]], that is, Israel according to the flesh and the letter, not according to the spirit and the spiritual interpretation, [[44:11|and thy father's house|et domum patris tui]], of whom thou wast begotten according to the flesh, so that thou mayest cleave in all things to the Father of spirits. For then [[44:12|the king shall greatly desire|concupiscet rex]], the Messias, the Only-begotten of God, [[44:12|thy beauty|decorem tuum]] within, namely thy humility, chastity and charity. For the Son of God so vehemently desired the beauty of Mary that he [[Ps 18:6|rejoiced as a giant to run the way|exsultaret quasi gigas ad currendam viam]], and came down into her most pure and most sweet womb, taking to himself from her a human body and uniting a part of her virginal substance to his divinity. Hence he says to her in the Canticle: [[Cant 2:14|shew me thy face, let thy voice sound in my ears: for thy voice is sweet, and thy face comely|Ostende mihi faciem tuam; sonet vox tua in auribus meis. Vox enim tua dulcis, et facies tua decora]]. O how greatly God has loved thee, most worthy Virgin! How most blessed art thou, my Lady, who wast found worthy to conceive the true God, to nourish him, to bear him, to handle him, to suckle him, to kiss him, to embrace him and to bring him up to his growth! Well couldst thou say that word of Solomon: [[Cant 7:10|I to my beloved, and his turning is towards me|Ego dilecto meo, et ad me conversio ejus]]; and that one also: [[Cant 1:12|A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, he shall abide between my breasts|Fasciculus myrrhæ dilectus meus mihi, inter ubera mea commorabitur]]. For indeed that young one, the most fair boy Jesus, often rested with thee on the flowery bed, slept, and sucked thy virgin breasts, looking on thee tenderly, kissing thee sweetly and embracing thee most reverently.

paras.t: Vultum tuum, o Domina, deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis. Beatam enim te dicunt omnes generationes, misericordiam tuam implorant, et ad te sicut ad benignissimam Advocatam in omni necessitate confugiunt. Adducentur regi virgines post eam. Omnes enim virgines ad Christum accedentes in via per fidem, et in patria per spem, Mariam tanquam primam et summam sequuntur, et ejus exemplo Christo obsequuntur.
paras.en: [[44:13|thy countenance|Vultum tuum]], O Lady, [[44:13|all the rich among the people, shall entreat|deprecabuntur omnes divites plebis]]. For all generations call thee blessed[[Luke 1:48||]] [the margin gives Luke i, 28; the words are those of Luke 1:48], implore thy mercy, and flee to thee as to a most kind Advocate in every need. [[44:15|After her shall virgins be brought to the king|Adducentur regi virgines post eam]]. For all virgins who come to Christ, on the way by faith and in the homeland by hope [so the text, *per spem*; one would expect *per speciem*, "by sight"], follow Mary as the first and highest, and by her example serve Christ.

paras.t: Ecce quam præclarissimus et gloriosissimus est psalmus iste. Et quæ lingua ejus præconium digne evolvat? Sed quoniam satis difficilis est, studeamus eum clare intelligere, itemque cum devotione decenti cantare.
paras.en: See how most excellent and most glorious this psalm is! And what tongue could worthily unfold its praise? But since it is rather difficult, let us strive to understand it clearly, and likewise to sing it with fitting devotion.

paras.t: Precatio. Fac nos, quæsumus, Deus Pater æterne, speciem et pulchritudinem unigeniti Filii tui diligere, ipsumque speciosum forma præ filiis hominum toto corde desiderare; et ut uncti oleo Sancti Spiritus, ipsius gratia semper tuis in oculis placeamus.
paras.en: Prayer. Make us, we beseech thee, O God, eternal Father, to love the comeliness and beauty of thy only-begotten Son, and with our whole heart to desire him who is [[44:3|beautiful above the sons of men|speciosum forma præ filiis hominum]]; and grant that, anointed with the oil of the Holy Ghost, we may by his grace be ever pleasing in thine eyes.

45.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUADRAGESIMI QUINTI : DEUS NOSTER REFUGIUM ET VIRTUS.
45.title_en: Exposition of the forty-fifth psalm: Our God is our refuge and strength.

paras.t: Habet denique psalmus modo tractandus hunc titulum: In finem, filiis Core, pro arcanis: id est, psalmus iste in Christum finem nostrum nos dirigens, convenit filiis Core, id est Christi fidelibus crucifixi vestigia digne sectantibus; pro arcanis, id est, psalmus iste tractat de secretis Christi mysteriis, scilicet de ejus adventu et incarnatione.
paras.en: Lastly, the psalm now to be treated has this title: [[45:1|Unto the end, for the sons of Core|In finem, filiis Core]], [[45:1|for the hidden|pro arcanis]]: that is, this psalm, directing us to Christ our end, befits the sons of Core, that is, the faithful of Christ who worthily follow the footsteps of the Crucified; [[45:1|for the hidden|pro arcanis]], that is, this psalm treats of the secret mysteries of Christ, namely of his coming and incarnation.

paras.t: In horum persona loquens Propheta, ait: Deus noster: de quo Moyses dicit: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies. Qui et alibi testatur: Videte quod ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me. Itaque iste Deus noster est refugium, ad quod in omni necessitate atque periculo fiducialiter accedere debemus, ut protegamur ab ipso. Ipse enim solus, et alius nullus, salvare nos potest ab omni discrimine: ideo sequitur, et virtus, id est, Deus noster est fortitudo nostra, seu forte atque omnipotens refugium ad se confugientium, quemadmodum inducitur: Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare non possit. Turris enim fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus et salvabitur. Quidam autem ad eos confugiunt, qui nec se ipsos, neque ad se confugientes valent salvare. De quibus scriptum est: Oculi impiorum deficient, et effugium peribit ab eis, et spes illorum abominatio erit. Tu ergo, propriam pensans insufficientiam, totam spem tuam in Domino fige, recolens quod Dominus ait: Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum. Ideo autem Job: Ecce, inquit, non est auxilium mihi in me. Insuper Deus noster est adjutor in tribulationibus, sicut asseritur: Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis. Unde et infra habetur: Invoca me in die tribulationis, et eruam te. Deus igitur est adjutor noster in tribulationibus, quæ invenerunt nos nimis, id est, quæ abundanter venerunt super nos. Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, persecutionem patientur. Et: Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis. In tribulationibus namque promptissimus est Deus ad succurrendum.
paras.en: Speaking in the person of these, the Prophet says: [[45:2|Our God|Deus noster]]: of whom Moses says: [[Deut 6:13|Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and shalt serve him only|Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies]] [Denis's wording, "Thou shalt adore", is that of Matt 4:10, where Christ quotes this verse]. And he also testifies elsewhere: [[Deut 32:39|See ye that I alone am, and there is no other God besides me|Videte quod ego sim solus, et non sit alius Deus præter me]]. So this God of ours is our [[45:2|refuge|refugium]], to which we ought to go with confidence in every need and danger, so as to be protected by him. For he alone, and no other, can save us from every peril: therefore there follows [[45:2|and strength|et virtus]], that is, our God is our strength, or the strong and almighty refuge of those who flee to him, as is set down: [[Is 59:1|Behold the hand of the Lord is not shortened that it cannot save|Ecce non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare non possit]]. For [[Prov 18:10|The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the just runneth to it|Turris enim fortissima nomen Domini; ad ipsum currit justus]], and shall be saved [the Vulgate has "and shall be exalted"]. But some flee to those who can save neither themselves nor those who flee to them. Of these it is written: [[Job 11:20|the eyes of the wicked shall decay, and the way to escape shall fail them, and their hope|Oculi impiorum deficient, et effugium peribit ab eis, et spes illorum]] shall be an abomination. Do thou therefore, weighing thine own insufficiency, fix all thy hope in the Lord, remembering what the Lord says: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me|Perditio tua, Israel, ex te; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]. And therefore Job: [[Job 6:13|Behold|Ecce]], he says, [[Job 6:13|there is no help for me in myself|non est auxilium mihi in me]]. Moreover our God is [[45:2|a helper in troubles|adjutor in tribulationibus]], as is affirmed: [[Nah 1:7|The Lord is good, and giveth strength in the day of trouble|Bonus Dominus et confortans in die tribulationis]]. Hence it is also said below: [[Ps 49:15|call upon me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee|Invoca me in die tribulationis, et eruam te]]. God therefore is our helper in troubles, [[45:2|which have found us exceedingly|quæ invenerunt nos nimis]], that is, which have come upon us abundantly. For [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ|Omnes enim qui volunt pie vivere in Christo]] [[2 Tim 3:12|shall suffer persecution|persecutionem patientur]]. And: [[Job 14:1|Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries|Homo natus de muliere, brevi vivens tempore, repletur multis miseriis]]. For in troubles God is most ready to come to our aid.

paras.t: Porro quæ sequuntur, multipliciter exponuntur. Possunt autem litteraliter ita exponi: Propterea non timebimus dum turbabitur terra, et transferentur montes in cor maris: id est, quoniam Deus noster est nostrum refugium, nostra virtus, et noster adjutor, idcirco non timebimus, quamvis terra moveatur vehementer, et montes transferantur in profundum abyssi seu medium pelagi violenter: quia (ut ait Apostolus) Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos? Et scriptum est: Qui timet Deum, nihil trepidabit. Ecce quanta est securitas mentis in Deo sperantis, quanta stabilitas cordis in Deum credentis. In nullo enim eventu pavebit, cujus animus in Deo veraciter fixus est. — Secundo sic: Non timebimus, nos in Deo confisi, dum turbabitur terra, id est homines terreni, qui temporalia damna atque tormenta corporalia timent: qui et in die judicii turbantur timore horribili, quando justi in magna constantia stabunt: secundum quod scriptum est, In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur, et de furore Omnipotentis bibet. Et transferentur montes in cor maris: id est, nec tunc timebimus, quando superbi projicientur in lacum inferni, quum dicet eis Judex, Ite, maledicti, in ignem æternum. Tunc enim justi cum securitate et gaudio audient, Venite, benedicti Patris mei.
paras.en: Now what follows is expounded in many ways. It can be expounded literally thus: [[45:3|Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled; and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea|Propterea non timebimus dum turbabitur terra, et transferentur montes in cor maris]]: that is, since our God is our refuge, our strength and our helper, therefore we will not fear, even though the earth be shaken violently and the mountains be carried with violence into the depth of the abyss or the midst of the ocean: because (as the Apostle says) [[Rom 8:31|If God be for us, who is against us?|Si Deus pro nobis, quis contra nos?]] And it is written: [[Ecclus 34:16|He that feareth the Lord shall tremble at nothing|Qui timet Deum, nihil trepidabit]]. See how great is the security of the mind that hopes in God, how great the steadfastness of the heart that believes in God. For he whose mind is truly fixed in God will be afraid at no event. Secondly thus: [[45:3|we will not fear|Non timebimus]], we who trust in God, [[45:3|when the earth shall be troubled|dum turbabitur terra]], that is, earthly men, who fear temporal losses and bodily torments; who also on the day of judgment are troubled with horrible fear[[Wis 5:2||]], when the just shall stand with great constancy[[Wis 5:1||]]: according as it is written: [[Job 21:30|the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath|In diem perditionis servatur malus, et ad diem furoris ducetur]], [[Job 21:20|and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty|et de furore Omnipotentis bibet]]. [[45:3|And the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea|Et transferentur montes in cor maris]]: that is, nor shall we fear then, when the proud shall be cast into the pit of hell, when the Judge shall say to them: Go, [[Matt 25:41|you cursed, into everlasting fire|maledicti, in ignem æternum]]. For then the just shall hear with security and joy: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]].

paras.t: Tertio sic, ut ea quæ dicta sunt, sint verba primitivæ Ecclesiæ, quæ totam fiduciam suam in Domino collocavit, et ait: Propterea non timebimus, timore carnali, humano et inordinato, dum turbabitur terra, id est Judæa seu populus Judæorum, qui Christi discipulos ex irrationabili perturbatione passionum conabantur omnino delere et exstirpare. Unde de primitiva Ecclesia legitur, quod ita orabant, quum principes sacerdotum prohibuissent prædicari nomen Domini Jesu: Da servis tuis, Domine, cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum. Et quum orassent, motus est locus in quo erant; et repleti sunt omnes Spiritu Sancto, et loquebantur verbum Dei cum fiducia. Et transferentur montes in cor maris: id est, nec tunc metuemus dum Apostoli, qui propter altitudinem vitæ et sapientiæ montes dicuntur, Judæam relinquent, et ad gentiles convertendos transibunt. Gentiles enim in corde maris, id est in medio mundi, habitabant: de quo infra habetur, Hoc mare magnum et spatiosum manibus; et iterum, Veni in altitudinem maris. Patet itaque quod tempore divisionis Apostolorum, Christiani in Jerusalem cum Jacobo permanentes, securi atque imperterriti permanserunt, certi quod Christus protector eorum esset. Unde et beatus frater Domini Jacobus, sæculares homines parvi pendens, et Christi famulos omnia contemnentes beatificans, ait: Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis. Thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus. Deinde fidelibus loquens: Patientes, inquit, estote usque ad adventum Domini, et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit.
paras.en: Thirdly thus, so that what has been said are the words of the primitive Church, which placed all its confidence in the Lord, and says: [[45:3|Therefore we will not fear|Propterea non timebimus]], with a carnal, human and inordinate fear, [[45:3|when the earth shall be troubled|dum turbabitur terra]], that is, Judea or the people of the Jews, who out of an unreasoning disturbance of the passions strove to blot out and root up the disciples of Christ altogether. Hence we read of the primitive Church that, when the chief priests had forbidden the name of the Lord Jesus to be preached, they prayed thus: O Lord, [[Acts 4:29|grant unto thy servants that with all confidence they may speak thy word|Da servis tuis, Domine, cum omni fiducia loqui verbum tuum]]. [[Acts 4:31|And when they had prayed, the place was moved wherein they were|Et quum orassent, motus est locus in quo erant]]; [[Acts 4:31|and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost: and they spoke the word of God with confidence|et repleti sunt omnes Spiritu Sancto, et loquebantur verbum Dei cum fiducia]]. [[45:3|And the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea|Et transferentur montes in cor maris]]: that is, nor shall we be afraid then, when the Apostles, who for the height of their life and wisdom are called mountains, shall leave Judea and pass over to convert the gentiles. For the gentiles dwelt in the heart of the sea, that is, in the midst of the world: of which it is said below, [[Ps 103:25|So is this great sea, which stretcheth wide its arms|Hoc mare magnum et spatiosum manibus]]; and again, [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]]. It is clear, then, that at the time of the dispersal of the Apostles [*divisio Apostolorum*: their parting to preach in different lands], the Christians who stayed in Jerusalem with James remained secure and undaunted, certain that Christ was their protector. Hence blessed James also, the brother of the Lord, making little of worldly men and calling blessed the servants of Christ who despise all things, says: [[Jas 5:1|Go to now, ye rich men: weep and howl in your miseries, which shall come upon you|Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis quæ advenient vobis]]. [[Jas 5:3|You have stored up to yourselves wrath against the last days|Thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus]]. Then, speaking to the faithful: [[Jas 5:7|Be patient|Patientes]], he says, [[Jas 5:7|until the coming of the Lord|estote usque ad adventum Domini]], [[Jas 5:8|and strengthen your hearts: for the coming of the Lord is at hand|et confirmate corda vestra, quoniam adventus Domini appropinquabit]].

paras.t: Sonuerunt montes prædicti, id est, sancti Apostoli Evangelium Christi prædicaverunt, et turbatæ sunt aquæ eorum: id est, gentes ad quas missi erant Apostoli, audita prædicatione eorum, turbatæ sunt: quædam ad impatientiam et persecutionem, quædam ad pœnitentiam et imitationem, sicut in Actibus Apostolorum frequenter narratur. Conturbati sunt montes, id est principales inter homines, in fortitudine ejus, scilicet Christi, id est ex potenti prædicatione et miraculosis operibus Apostolorum, ac aliorum Christi discipulorum. Hæc autem conturbatio accipi potest in bono et in malo. Nam quidam potentes et magni ad fidem conversi sunt, tam ex Judæis quam ex paganis, quemadmodum scriptum est: Multa etiam turba sacerdotum obediebat Evangelio. Quidam quoque timore ingenti turbati sunt, teste Luca: Multa, inquit, prodigia et signa fiebant per Apostolos in Jerusalem, et metus magnus erat in universis. Quidam et plures prioribus conturbati sunt conturbatione maligna, videlicet perversi principes Judæorum atque tyranni gentilium. Pro majori equidem parte montes sæculi, id est potentes ac nobiles, in sua malitia permanserunt. Propter quod Apostolus ait: Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles sunt inter vos. Et Jacobus: Nonne, inquit, Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo, divites in fide? Omnes autem montes, id est superbi Deo rebelles, turbati sunt vel in præsenti, vel in futuro, imo et utrobique: quoniam nusquam veram pacem habent, qui Deo resistunt, juxta illud: Sapiens corde est Deus et fortis robore. Quis restitit ei, et pacem habuit? Et per Isaiam Dominus dicit: Ultionem capiam, et non resistet mihi homo. Et alibi: Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me? ait Dominus. Et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo?
paras.en: The aforesaid mountains [[45:4|roared|Sonuerunt]] [the Latin *sonuerunt*, "they sounded", is here taken with the mountains as its subject], that is, the holy Apostles preached the Gospel of Christ, [[45:4|and were troubled|et turbatæ sunt]], namely [[45:4|their waters|aquæ eorum]]: that is, the nations to whom the Apostles had been sent, having heard their preaching, were troubled: some unto impatience and persecution, some unto penance and imitation, as is often related in the Acts of the Apostles. [[45:4|The mountains were troubled|Conturbati sunt montes]], that is, the chief among men, [[45:4|with his strength|in fortitudine ejus]], namely Christ's, that is, by the mighty preaching and miraculous works of the Apostles and of the other disciples of Christ. Now this troubling can be taken in a good sense and in a bad. For some of the mighty and great were converted to the faith, both of the Jews and of the pagans, as it is written: [[Acts 6:7|A great multitude also of the priests obeyed|Multa etiam turba sacerdotum obediebat]] the Gospel. Some too were troubled with a great fear, as Luke testifies: [[Acts 2:43|Many wonders also and signs were done by the apostles in Jerusalem|Multa, inquit, prodigia et signa fiebant per Apostolos in Jerusalem]], and great fear was upon all [the margin gives Acts ii, 44; the verse is Acts 2:43, where the Douay-Rheims has "great fervor" for *metus magnus*]. And others, more than the former, were troubled with a malignant troubling, namely the perverse princes of the Jews and the tyrants of the gentiles. For the greater part, indeed, the mountains of the world, that is, the mighty and the noble, remained in their malice. For which reason the Apostle says: [[1 Cor 1:26|see your vocation, brethren, that there are not many wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble|Videte vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobiles]] among you. And James: [[Jas 2:5|Hath not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith|Nonne, inquit, Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo, divites in fide?]]? But all the mountains, that is, the proud who rebel against God, are troubled either in the present or in the future, nay in both: since those who resist God nowhere have true peace, according to that saying: [[Job 9:4|He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath resisted him, and hath had peace?|Sapiens corde est Deus et fortis robore. Quis restitit ei, et pacem habuit?]] [Denis adds *Deus*: "God is wise in heart"]. And through Isaias the Lord says: [[Is 47:3|I will take vengeance, and no man shall resist me|Ultionem capiam, et non resistet mihi homo]]. And elsewhere: [[Jer 49:19|who is like to me? and who shall abide me?|Quis similis mei? et quis sustinebit me?]] says the Lord, [[Jer 49:19|and who is that shepherd that can withstand my countenance?|Et quis est iste pastor qui resistat vultui meo?]]

paras.t: Si autem quis velit ista ad litteram in sensu grammaticali accipere, tunc palam est quod etiam divina virtute montes terræ suo modo turbantur, et de locis suis transferuntur ac comminuuntur, secundum quod in libro Job legitur: Qui transtulit montes, et commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutientur. Et Salvator ait: Habete fidem Dei. Amen dico vobis, quia quicumque dixerit huic monti, Tollere, et mittere in mare; et non hæsitaverit in corde suo, sed crediderit quia quodcumque dixerit fiat, fiet ei. Omnia enim (sicut scribit Marcus) possibilia sunt credenti.
paras.en: But if anyone wishes to take these words according to the letter, in the grammatical sense, then it is plain that by the divine power the mountains of the earth too are in their own way troubled, and removed from their places and broken in pieces, according to what is read in the book of Job: [[Job 9:5|Who hath removed mountains|Qui transtulit montes]], [[Job 9:6|who shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble|et commovet terram de loco suo, et columnæ ejus concutientur]]. And the Saviour says: [[Mark 11:22|Have the faith of God|Habete fidem Dei]]. [[Mark 11:23|Amen I say to you that whosoever shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed and be cast into the sea, and shall not stagger in his heart, but be believe that whatsoever he saith shall be done; it shall be done unto him|Amen dico vobis, quia quicumque dixerit huic monti, Tollere, et mittere in mare; et non hæsitaverit in corde suo, sed crediderit quia quodcumque dixerit fiat, fiet ei]]. For [[Mark 9:22|all things|Omnia]] (as Mark writes) [[Mark 9:22|are possible to him that believeth|possibilia sunt credenti]].

paras.t: Fluminis impetus, id est fons sacri Baptismatis, lætificat, spirituali lætitia, civitatem Dei, id est militantem Ecclesiam Christi. Gaudent enim fideles de sacramento ac beneficio tanto, in quo omnia peccata donantur, gratiæ infunduntur, et homo spiritualiter regeneratur. De hoc fluminis impetu scriptum est: Ecce aquæ egrediebantur subter limen domus ad orientem; et omnis anima vivens quæ serpit, quocumque venerit torrens, vivet. Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum, id est Ecclesiam electorum, seu ipsos electos, Altissimus Deus, qui solus potest facere mundum de immundo. De hoc tabernaculo ait Apostolus: Vos estis templum Dei vivi, sicut dicit Dominus: Quoniam inhabitabo in illis. Et iterum ait: Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos.
paras.en: [[45:5|The stream of the river|Fluminis impetus]], that is, the font of holy Baptism, [[45:5|maketh the city of God joyful|lætificat, spirituali lætitia, civitatem Dei]] with a spiritual joy, that is, the Church of Christ militant. For the faithful rejoice in so great a sacrament and benefit, in which all sins are forgiven, graces are infused, and man is spiritually reborn. Of this stream of the river it is written: [[Ezech 47:1|behold waters issued out from under the threshold of the house toward the east|Ecce aquæ egrediebantur subter limen domus ad orientem]]; [[Ezech 47:9|And every living creature that creepeth whithersoever the torrent shall come, shall live|et omnis anima vivens quæ serpit, quocumque venerit torrens, vivet]]. He [[45:5|hath sanctified his own tabernacle|Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum]], that is, the Church of the elect, or the elect themselves, namely [[45:5|the most High|Altissimus]] God, who alone can make clean what is unclean[[Job 14:4||]]. Of this tabernacle the Apostle says: [[2 Cor 6:16|you are the temple of the living God|Vos estis templum Dei vivi]], as the Lord saith: [[2 Cor 6:16|I will dwell in them|Quoniam inhabitabo in illis]][[Lev 26:12||]]. And again he says: [[1 Cor 3:17|the temple of God is holy, which you are|Templum Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos]].

paras.t: Deus in medio ejus non commovebitur. Hoc dupliciter legitur. Primo sic: Deus in medio ejus, subaudi, est, id est in ipsa civitate seu militanti Ecclesia, juxta illud: Ubi sunt duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi sum in medio eorum; non commovebitur, id est, Ecclesia non cadet a fide, eo quod Christus in medio ejus sit, nec tentationibus dejicietur, secundum quod Christus Petro in persona Ecclesiæ dixit: Ecce Satanas expetivit vos ut cribraret sicut triticum; ego autem oravi pro te, ut non deficiat fides tua. Adjuvabit eam, scilicet Ecclesiam, Deus mane, id est statim quum ad eum clamaverit, diluculo, id est in spirituali aurora, utpote in infusione gratiæ, seu Spiritus Sancti illuminatione.
paras.en: [[45:6|God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved|Deus in medio ejus non commovebitur]]. This is read in two ways. First thus: [[45:6|God is in the midst thereof|Deus in medio ejus]], supply *is* [the Latin has no verb here: "God in the midst of it"], that is, in that city or Church militant, according to that saying: [[Matt 18:20|where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them|Ubi sunt duo vel tres congregati in nomine meo, ibi sum in medio eorum]]; [[45:6|it shall not be moved|non commovebitur]], that is, the Church shall not fall from the faith, because Christ is in her midst, nor shall she be cast down by temptations, according to what Christ said to Peter in the person of the Church: [[Luke 22:31|behold Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat|Ecce Satanas expetivit vos ut cribraret sicut triticum]]; [[Luke 22:32|But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not|ego autem oravi pro te, ut non deficiat fides tua]]. [[45:6|God will help it|Adjuvabit eam]], namely the Church, [[45:6|in the morning|mane]], that is, at once when she cries to him, [[45:6|early|diluculo]], that is, in the spiritual dawn, as in the infusion of grace, or the enlightening of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Denique locus iste potest anagogice explanari, ut sit sensus: Fluminis impetus, id est fons sapientiæ, seu inundatio Spiritus Sancti, vel ipsemet Deus, qui (ut scriptum est) est fluvius gloriosus, exsiliens in terram sitientem, lætificat, lætitia beatificæ fruitionis, civitatem Dei, id est triumphantem Ecclesiam. Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum, id est corda Beatorum, Altissimus: nil enim impuritatis esse potest in patria. Deus in medio ejus est: quia in triumphanti Ecclesia Deus facie ad faciem cernitur, quemadmodum Isaias ait, Erit tibi Dominus in lucem perpetuam: idcirco non commovebitur Ecclesia triumphans a suæ beatitudinis statu, sed æternaliter Deo fruetur. Adjuvabit eam, id est civitatem cœlestem, Deus mane diluculo, id est, mox quum aliquem Sanctorum ad cœlos susceperit, confirmabit eum in bono, ut amplius peccare non queat.
paras.en: Lastly, this passage can be explained anagogically [that is, of the glory of heaven], so that the sense is: [[45:5|The stream of the river|Fluminis impetus]], that is, the fountain of wisdom, or the flood of the Holy Ghost, or God himself, who (as it is written) is a glorious river, leaping forth upon the thirsty land[[Amos 8:8||]] [the margin gives Amos viii, 8, and a marginal variant reads *universus*, "whole", for *gloriosus*, as in Amos 8:8, *quasi fluvius universus*; that verse does not otherwise fit, and the source of Denis's words is uncertain], [[45:5|maketh the city of God joyful|lætificat civitatem Dei]] with the joy of beatific fruition, that is, the Church triumphant. He [[45:5|hath sanctified his own tabernacle|Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum]], that is, the hearts of the Blessed, namely [[45:5|the most High|Altissimus]]: for nothing impure can be in the fatherland. [[45:6|God is in the midst thereof|Deus in medio ejus]]: for in the Church triumphant God is seen face to face, as Isaias says: [[Is 60:19|the Lord shall be unto thee for an everlasting light|Erit tibi Dominus in lucem perpetuam]]: therefore the Church triumphant [[45:6|shall not be moved|non commovebitur]] from the state of her beatitude, but shall enjoy God eternally. [[45:6|God will help it|Adjuvabit eam]], that is, the heavenly city, [[45:6|in the morning early|mane diluculo]], that is, as soon as he has taken up any of the Saints to heaven, he will confirm him in good, so that he can sin no more.

paras.t: Præterea exponi potest hic passus de Virgine gloriosa, hoc modo: Fluminis impetus lætificat civitatem Dei: id est, Verbum Dei, in quo est omnium sanctarum deliciarum fontalis atque immensa affluentia, sanctam Mariam exsultare fecit, præsertim quando in uterum ejus cum omni sua plenitudine descendit, eamque superimplevit, atque humanam naturam ex ea vere assumpsit. Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum Altissimus. Nam Christus Matrem quam sibi elegit et condidit, ab omni immunditia culpæ purissimam præservavit, et eam in utero suæ matris sanctificavit, ac Spiritu Sancto implevit multo sublimius quam Jeremiam aut Joannem Baptistam. Deus in medio ejus: nam Christus Deus et homo in sacratissimo Virginis utero novem mensibus requievit. Ideo Virgo Christifera non commovebitur a bono in malum, sed stabilis erit in Deo atque immobilis. Adjuvabit eam Deus mane diluculo, id est, ex utero matris suæ stabilivit eam in omni perfectione ac gratia secundum actum vel habitum, seu dispositionem propinquam.
paras.en: Moreover this passage can be expounded of the glorious Virgin, in this way: [[45:5|The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful|Fluminis impetus lætificat civitatem Dei]]: that is, the Word of God, in whom is the fontal and boundless abundance of all holy delights, made holy Mary exult, above all when he descended into her womb with all his fulness, and filled her to overflowing, and truly took human nature from her. [[45:5|The most High hath sanctified his own tabernacle|Sanctificavit tabernaculum suum Altissimus]]. For Christ preserved the Mother whom he chose and made for himself most pure from every uncleanness of sin, and sanctified her in her mother's womb, and filled her with the Holy Ghost far more sublimely than Jeremias[[Jer 1:5||]] or John the Baptist[[Luke 1:15||]]. [[45:6|God is in the midst thereof|Deus in medio ejus]]: for Christ, God and man, rested nine months in the most sacred womb of the Virgin. Therefore the Christ-bearing Virgin [[45:6|shall not be moved|non commovebitur]] from good to evil, but shall be stable and immovable in God. [[45:6|God will help it in the morning early|Adjuvabit eam Deus mane diluculo]], that is, from her mother's womb he established her in all perfection and grace, in act or in habit, or in proximate disposition [that is, a readiness close to the act itself].

paras.t: Quod vero dictum est, Deus in medio ejus non commovebitur: secundo sic legitur, ut nihil subaudiatur, ut sit sensus: Deus non commovebitur in medio Ecclesiæ militantis, triumphantis, seu Mariæ virginis. Quamvis enim Deus in se ipso omnino impassibilis immobilisque consistat, solent tamen ei adscribi quædam ad passionem ac motum spectantia: quia circa rationalem creaturam ita se habet, quasi talia sibi vere competerent. Hinc enim apud Malachiam legitur: Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris. Sequenti quoque capitulo Dominus: Me, inquit, configitis gens tota. Invaluerunt super me verba vestra. Apostolus vero apertius ait: Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei. Simili modo dicitur Deus commoveri, quando a peccatore contemnitur et recedit; dum vero incessanter in aliquo per gratiam manet, dicitur non commoveri.
paras.en: As for the words [[45:6|God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved|Deus in medio ejus non commovebitur]], they are read in a second way, with nothing supplied, so that the sense is: God shall not be moved in the midst of the Church militant, or triumphant, or of the Virgin Mary. For although God in himself abides altogether impassible and immovable, yet certain things belonging to passion and motion are commonly ascribed to him, because towards the rational creature he behaves as though such things truly belonged to him. Hence we read in Malachias: [[Mal 2:17|You have wearied the Lord with your words|Laborare fecistis Dominum in sermonibus vestris]]. And in the following chapter the Lord says: [[Mal 3:9|you afflict me, even the whole nation of you|Me, inquit, configitis gens tota]] [*configitis*: literally "you pierce"]. [[Mal 3:13|Your words have been unsufferable to me|Invaluerunt super me verba vestra]]. And the Apostle says more plainly: [[Eph 4:30|grieve not the holy Spirit of God|Nolite contristare Spiritum Sanctum Dei]]. In like manner God is said to be moved when he is despised by the sinner and withdraws; but while he abides unceasingly in someone through grace, he is said not to be moved.

paras.t: Conturbatæ sunt gentes ex prædicatione atque miraculis discipulorum Salvatoris, ad pœnitentiam salutarem et admirationem; quædam vero ad obstinationem et resistentiam. Et inclinata sunt regna: id est, incolæ regnorum humiliati sunt ad fidem et sanctam conversationem, discentes a Christo quia mitis est et humilis corde. Hoc est quod beatissimus Isaias de Christo prædixit: Quia incurvabit habitantes in excelso, civitatem sublimem humiliabit. Per civitatem autem sublimem intelligit Romam, quæ tunc erat domina mundi. De qua Propheta idem subjungit: Conculcabit eam pes pauperis, gressus egenorum. Per pedem pauperis, Petrum piscatorem intellige; per gressum egenorum, prædicationem Petri et Pauli, nihil in hoc mundo possidere volentium. Horum enim prædicatio, infidelem gloriam Romanorum atque pomposam eorum sublimitatem, ad christianæ humilitatis profunditatem perduxit. Dedit vocem suam Christus, per se ipsum et prædicationem servorum suorum; mota est terra ad fidem et admirationem, vel etiam ad perturbationem et indurationem, maxime quoad Judæos: de quibus per Isaiam Christus testatur, Israel me non cognovit, et populus meus non intellexit. Hoc quoque quod ait, Mota est terra, convenienter refertur ad versum sequentem, quo dicitur:
paras.en: [[45:7|Nations were troubled|Conturbatæ sunt gentes]] by the preaching and miracles of the disciples of the Saviour, unto saving penance and wonder; but some unto obstinacy and resistance. [[45:7|And kingdoms were bowed down|Et inclinata sunt regna]]: that is, the inhabitants of kingdoms were humbled unto the faith and a holy way of life, learning from Christ that he is [[Matt 11:29|meek, and humble of heart|mitis est et humilis corde]]. This is what most blessed Isaias foretold of Christ: [[Is 26:5|For he shall bring down them that dwell on high, the high city he shall lay low|Quia incurvabit habitantes in excelso, civitatem sublimem humiliabit]]. By the high city he means Rome, which was then mistress of the world. Of which the same Prophet adds: [[Is 26:6|The foot shall tread it down|Conculcabit eam pes]] of the poor, [[Is 26:6|the steps of the needy|gressus egenorum]]. By the foot of the poor understand Peter the fisherman; by the steps of the needy, the preaching of Peter and Paul, who wished to possess nothing in this world. For their preaching brought down the faithless glory of the Romans and their pompous loftiness to the depth of Christian humility. [[45:7|He uttered his voice|Dedit vocem suam]], Christ, by himself and by the preaching of his servants; [[45:7|the earth trembled|mota est terra]] [*mota est*: literally "was moved"] unto faith and wonder, or else unto disturbance and hardening, above all as regards the Jews: of whom Christ testifies through Isaias, [[Is 1:3|Israel hath not known me, and my people hath not understood|Israel me non cognovit, et populus meus non intellexit]]. This too that he says, [[45:7|the earth trembled|Mota est terra]], is fittingly referred to the following verse, in which it is said:

paras.t: Dominus virtutum nobiscum: id est, Christus rex gloriæ, virtus et sapientia Patris, venit ad nos, et habitavit nobiscum per assumptionem carnis et animæ rationalis. Et ideo subdit, susceptor noster, id est, qui nostram naturam assumpsit, nosque redemit, est Deus Jacob patriarchæ, id est verus Deus, non pura creatura, ut hæretici asseruerunt. Huic autem expositioni concordat quod Dominus asserit: Adhuc unum modicum, et ego movebo cœlum et terram, et mare et aridam; et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus. Circa adventum enim et in adventu Christi motum est cœlum, quando angelo pastoribus Christi nativitatem annuntiante, facta est cum eo multitudo cœlestis exercitus, laudantium Deum et dicentium, Gloria in excelsis Deo; quando etiam stella ceteris radiantior Magis apparuit, eosque ad Creatorem cœlorum hominem factum perduxit. Terra vero mota est, quando omnes mirabantur propter ea quæ a pastoribus dicebantur. Mare vero et arida mota sunt ante Christi adventum, quando per dispensationem divinam potestati Romanorum subjecta sunt regna mundi et insulæ maris. Tunc igitur venit Desideratus cunctis gentibus, id est Christus: de quo Jacob prædixit, Ipse erit exspectatio gentium; de quo nunc quoque dicitur, Dominus virtutum nobiscum; de quo alibi scriptum est, Vocabitur nomen ejus Emmanuel, quod interpretatur, Nobiscum Deus.
paras.en: [[45:8|The Lord of armies is with us|Dominus virtutum nobiscum]]: that is, Christ the king of glory, the power and wisdom of the Father[[1 Cor 1:24||]], came to us and dwelt with us by taking flesh and a rational soul. And therefore he adds, [[45:8|our protector|susceptor noster]] [*susceptor*: literally "he who takes up"; Denis reads it of Christ's taking up our nature], that is, he who took our nature and redeemed us, is [[45:8|the God of Jacob|Deus Jacob]] the patriarch, that is, true God, not a mere creature, as the heretics asserted. With this exposition agrees what the Lord asserts: [[Agg 2:7|Yet one little while, and I will move the heaven and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land|Adhuc unum modicum, et ego movebo cœlum et terram, et mare et aridam]]; [[Agg 2:8|and the desired of all nations shall come|et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]. For about the coming of Christ, and at his coming, the heaven was moved, when, as the angel announced Christ's birth to the shepherds, there was with him [[Luke 2:13|a multitude of the heavenly army, praising God and saying|multitudo cœlestis exercitus, laudantium Deum et dicentium]], [[Luke 2:14|Glory to God in the highest|Gloria in excelsis Deo]]; when also a star more radiant than the rest appeared to the Magi, and led them to the Creator of the heavens made man[[Matt 2:2||]][[Matt 2:9||]][[Matt 2:11||]]. And the earth was moved when all wondered at the things that were told by the shepherds[[Luke 2:18||]]. And the sea and the dry land were moved before the coming of Christ, when by divine dispensation the kingdoms of the world and the islands of the sea were made subject to the power of the Romans. Then, therefore, came the Desired of all nations, that is, Christ: of whom Jacob foretold, [[Gen 49:10|he shall be the expectation of nations|Ipse erit exspectatio gentium]]; of whom it is now also said, [[45:8|The Lord of armies is with us|Dominus virtutum nobiscum]]; of whom it is written elsewhere, [[Is 7:14|his name shall be called Emmanuel|Vocabitur nomen ejus Emmanuel]], [[Matt 1:23|which being interpreted is, God with us|quod interpretatur, Nobiscum Deus]].

paras.t: Moraliter denique, Dominus virtutum, id est Deus Trinitas, est nobiscum, quando per caritatem et gratiam in nostris cordibus manet; et susceptor noster, id est orationum nostrarum auditor, est Deus Jacob, id est supplantatoris vitiorum. Qui enim vitiis reluctantur, exaudiri merentur, non quorum propositum in vitio manet. Propter quod cæcus apud Joannem aiebat: Scimus quoniam peccatores Deus non audit; sed si quis Dei cultor est, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit. Cui consonat quod alibi ait Scriptura: Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis.
paras.en: Morally, lastly: [[45:8|The Lord of armies|Dominus virtutum]], that is, God the Trinity, is [[45:8|with us|nobiscum]] when he abides in our hearts through charity and grace; and [[45:8|our protector|susceptor noster]], that is, the hearer of our prayers, is [[45:8|the God of Jacob|Deus Jacob]], that is, of the supplanter of vices [*Jacob* is interpreted "supplanter"; see Gen 27:36]. For those who struggle against vices deserve to be heard, not those whose purpose remains in vice. For which reason the blind man in John said: [[John 9:31|we know that God doth not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and doth his, will, him he heareth|Scimus quoniam peccatores Deus non audit; sed si quis Dei cultor est, et voluntatem ejus facit, hunc exaudit]]. With which agrees what Scripture says elsewhere: [[Job 8:20|God will not cast away the simple, nor reach out his hand to the evil doer|Deus non projiciet simplicem, nec porriget manum malignis]].

paras.t: Venite, non tam gressibus pedum, quam fide affectuque cordium; et videte oculo mentis, o omnes qui vultis salvari, opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram, id est mirabilia opera Creatoris facta in terris. De quibus subjungitur: auferens bella usque ad finem terræ. In Christi enim adventu inaudita pax erat in mundo omnibus populis Romano imperio subditis: quod utique non humana, sed divina ordinatione atque potentia factum est, non propter meritum Romanorum tunc exsistentium, sed propter futuros electos. Arcum conteret, et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni: id est, pax ista insolita tam diu durabit, quod usus armorum ultra solitum tempus cessabit; sicque Deo disponente, homines bellica instrumenta in alios usus convertent, sicut quotidie fit in terris in quibus bella longo tempore conquiescunt. Et hoc est quod alibi dicitur: De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Et conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces. Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium. Hoc enim dicitur eo modo, quo de aliqua re ultra solitum perdurante dicimus, Istud nunquam habebit finem, quum tamen quandoque infra diem vel mensem seu horam habiturum sit finem.
paras.en: [[45:9|Come|Venite]], not so much with the steps of the feet as with the faith and affection of the heart; [[45:9|and behold ye|et videte]] with the eye of the mind, O all you who wish to be saved, [[45:9|the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth|opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram]], that is, the wonderful works of the Creator done on earth. Of which there is added: [[45:10|Making wars to cease even to the end of the earth|auferens bella usque ad finem terræ]]. For at the coming of Christ there was an unheard-of peace in the world among all the peoples subject to the Roman empire: which was surely brought about not by human but by divine ordinance and power, not for the merit of the Romans then living, but for the sake of the elect who were to come. [[45:10|He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield he shall burn in the fire|Arcum conteret, et confringet arma, et scuta comburet igni]]: that is, this unwonted peace will last so long that the use of arms will cease beyond the usual time; and so, by God's disposing, men will turn the instruments of war to other uses, as happens every day in lands where wars are long at rest. And this is what is said elsewhere: [[Is 2:3|the law shall come forth from Sion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem|De Sion exibit lex, et verbum Domini de Jerusalem]]. [[Is 2:4|and they shall turn their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into sickles: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they be exercised any more to war|Et conflabunt gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces. Non levabit gens contra gentem gladium, nec exercebuntur ultra ad prælium]][[Mich 4:2||]] [the margin also gives Mich. iv, 2, where the same prophecy stands]. For this is said in the way in which we say of something lasting beyond the usual, This will never have an end, though in fact it will have an end at some time, within a day or a month or an hour.

paras.t: Potest autem hic locus spiritualiter interpretari, ut sit sensus: Venite, et videte opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram, id est, incarnationem Filii, partum Virginis, passionem et resurrectionem Salvatoris: qui est auferens bella usque ad finem terræ, id est, qui tentationes a nobis excludit, et homines Deo reconciliavit. Ipse est enim pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, id est, gentiles atque Judæos in unitate fidei congregavit: quemadmodum legitur, Pax erit inter duos illos; et secundum Apostolum, Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi. Arcum conteret, id est, Christus occultas malorum insidias condemnabit ac destruet, et confringet arma, id est persecutiones apertas ac invasiones diabolicas; et scuta, id est defensiones fallaces, quibus perversi suos conantur errores defendere, comburet igni infernali, damnando perversos, vel igne Spiritus Sancti, illuminando fideles ad resistendum errantibus.
paras.en: This place can also be interpreted spiritually, so that the sense is: [[45:9|Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders he hath done upon earth|Venite, et videte opera Domini, quæ posuit prodigia super terram]], that is, the incarnation of the Son, the Virgin's childbearing, the passion and resurrection of the Saviour: who is the one [[45:10|making wars to cease even to the end of the earth|auferens bella usque ad finem terræ]], that is, who shuts temptations out from us, and reconciled men to God. [[Eph 2:14|For he is our peace, who hath made both one|Ipse est enim pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]], that is, he gathered gentiles and Jews together in the unity of faith: as we read, There shall be peace between those two[[Zach 6:13||]] [Denis gives the words in brief; the Douay-Rheims has "the counsel of peace shall be between them both"]; and, according to the Apostle, [[2 Cor 5:19|God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself|Deus erat in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi]]. [[45:10|He shall destroy the bow|Arcum conteret]], that is, Christ will condemn and destroy the hidden snares of the wicked, [[45:10|and break the weapons|et confringet arma]], that is, open persecutions and the assaults of the devil; [[45:10|and the shield|et scuta]], that is, the false defences by which the perverse try to defend their errors, [[45:10|he shall burn in the fire|comburet igni]] of hell, by damning the perverse, or with the fire of the Holy Ghost, by enlightening the faithful to resist those in error.

paras.t: Vacate, et videte quoniam ego sum Deus. Ecce quam pie ac dulciter exhortatur nos Dominus Deus noster. Vacate, inquit, id est, a rebus vanis et malis ac inutilibus abstrahite corda vestra, et mihi tota mente adhærete, mihi intendite, in me vestra desideria figite, in me vestras occupationes simplificate ac colligite; et videte per affectuosam contemplationem, experimentalemque gustum, quoniam ego sum Deus creator, provisor, salvator et rector vester, qui incessabilem curam de vobis habeo, vobisque semper succurrere, et consolationem infundere paratus exsisto, ita ut experimentaliter agnoscatis me esse Deum vestrum. Qui enim ista gustare et Deo sincere intendere cupit, indiget omni custodia cor suum servare, concupiscentias fugere, voluptates contemnere, dissolutiones vitare, occupationes superfluas propulsare, loquacitates abjicere, et illud unum quod solum necessarium est, indesinenter appetere. Ideo Jeremias præcipit: Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas. Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum.
paras.en: [[45:11|Be still and see that I am God|Vacate, et videte quoniam ego sum Deus]]. See how lovingly and sweetly the Lord our God exhorts us. [[45:11|Be still|Vacate]], he says [the Latin *vacate* is "be free", "be at leisure": empty yourselves of other things for God], that is, withdraw your hearts from vain and evil and useless things, and cleave to me with your whole mind, attend to me, fix your desires on me, make your occupations simple and gather them up in me; [[45:11|and see|et videte]] by loving contemplation and the taste of experience, [[45:11|that I am God|quoniam ego sum Deus]], your creator, provider, saviour and ruler, who have unceasing care of you, and am ever ready to come to your aid and pour consolation into you, so that you may know by experience that I am your God. For he who desires to taste these things and to attend sincerely to God needs to keep his heart with all watchfulness[[Prov 4:23||]], to flee concupiscences, despise pleasures, avoid dissipations, drive away superfluous occupations, cast off talkativeness, and unceasingly seek that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. Therefore Jeremias commands: [[Jer 4:3|Break up anew your fallow ground, and sow not upon thorns|Novate vobis novale, et nolite serere super spinas]]. [[Jer 4:4|Be circumcised to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your hearts|Circumcidimini Domino, et auferte præputia cordium vestrorum]].

paras.t: Exaltabor in gentibus, id est, ego Unigenitus Dei ac mundi Salvator a gentibus agnoscar, et honorabor per prædicationem Apostolorum: secundum quod Isaias prædixit: Quibus non est annuntiatum de eo, videbunt; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt. Et iterum: Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri. Et denuo: In doctrinis glorificate Dominum. A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi. Et per alium Prophetam Christus ait: Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus. De quo et Michæas prædixit: Magnificabitur in medio universæ terræ. Et exaltabor in terra, id est in populo Judæorum in fine sæculi. Quum enim plenitudo gentium intraverit, tunc omnis Israel salvus fiet. Nam usque ad finem mundi durabit Judæorum cæcitas, atque captivitas, juxta illud: Finis ejus vastitas, et usque ad finem perseverabit desolatio. Circa finem autem sæculi convertentur adveniente Elia, quemadmodum Dominus ait: Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis; et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres eorum, ne forte veniam, et percutiam terram anathemate.
paras.en: [[45:11|I will be exalted among the nations|Exaltabor in gentibus]], that is, I, the Only-begotten of God and Saviour of the world, shall be acknowledged by the gentiles, and honoured through the preaching of the Apostles: according as Isaias foretold: [[Is 52:15|they to whom it was not told of him, have seen: and they that heard not, have beheld|Quibus non est annuntiatum de eo, videbunt; et qui non audierunt, contemplati sunt]] [Denis has the future, "shall see"]. And again: [[Is 52:10|all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God|Videbunt omnes fines terræ salutare Dei nostri]]. And once more: [[Is 24:15|glorify ye the Lord in instruction|In doctrinis glorificate Dominum]]. [[Is 24:16|From the ends of the earth we have heard praises, the glory of the just one|A finibus terræ audivimus laudes, gloriam Justi]]. And through another Prophet Christ says: [[Mal 1:11|from the rising of the sun even to the going down, my name is great among the Gentiles|Ab ortu solis usque ad occasum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus]]. Of whom Micheas too foretold: He shall be magnified in the midst of the whole earth[[Mich 5:4||]] [the Vulgate has "even to the ends of the earth"]. [[45:11|And I will be exalted in the earth|Et exaltabor in terra]], that is, among the people of the Jews, at the end of the world. For when [[Rom 11:25|the fulness of the Gentiles|plenitudo gentium]] shall have come in, then [[Rom 11:26|all Israel|omnis Israel]] shall be saved. For the blindness and captivity of the Jews will last until the end of the world, according to that saying: [[Dan 9:26|the end thereof shall be waste|Finis ejus vastitas]], and even to the end [[Dan 9:27|the desolation shall continue|perseverabit desolatio]]. But about the end of the world they will be converted at the coming of Elias, as the Lord says: [[Mal 4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias the prophet, before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord|Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam, antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]]; [[Mal 4:6|And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers: lest I come, and strike the earth with anathema|et convertet cor patrum ad filios, et cor filiorum ad patres eorum, ne forte veniam, et percutiam terram anathemate]].

paras.t: Dominus virtutum nobiscum, etc. Versus iste propter significationis suæ dulcedinem ac dignitatem repetitur: qui jam satis declaratus videtur.
paras.en: [[45:12|The Lord of armies is with us|Dominus virtutum nobiscum]], etc. This verse is repeated because of the sweetness and dignity of its meaning; it seems already to have been sufficiently explained.

paras.t: Ecce quam plenus est hic psalmus sacramentis: in quo fides roboratur, spes in Deo stabilitur, fortitudo excitatur, nascentis Ecclesiæ primordia explicantur, Baptismi gratia commendatur, beneficia Dei recoluntur, Christi incarnatio designatur, fideles ad considerationem divinorum operum invitantur, divina potentia prædicatur, dulcissima atque paterna Dei admonitio continetur, Salvatoris magnificentia prædicatur, atque ad primum ac summum et suavissimum Dei beneficium, scilicet ad incarnationem ipsius, redit: et in hoc beneficio psalmus finitur, ne aliquo modo oblivioni tradatur. Enitamur ergo psalmum tam fecundum ac pulchrum devotissime decantare.
paras.en: See how full of mysteries this psalm is [*sacramentis*: sacred mysteries, signs of hidden things]: in it faith is strengthened, hope is established in God, fortitude is roused, the beginnings of the infant Church are set forth, the grace of Baptism is commended, the benefits of God are recalled, the incarnation of Christ is signified, the faithful are invited to consider the divine works, the divine power is proclaimed, the most sweet and fatherly admonition of God is contained, the magnificence of the Saviour is proclaimed; and it returns to the first, highest and sweetest benefit of God, namely his incarnation: and the psalm ends with this benefit, lest it be in any way forgotten. Let us strive, then, to sing this psalm, so fruitful and so beautiful, most devoutly.

paras.t: Precatio. Deus Jacob et Domine virtutum, arcum nobis adversantium contere, et eorum arma nequissima contra nos confringe: ut tua virtute ablatis bellis, perenniter tibi vacemus, et videamus quoniam tu es Deus.
paras.en: Prayer. O [[45:8|God of Jacob|Deus Jacob]] and [[45:8|Lord of armies|Domine virtutum]], destroy [[45:10|the bow|arcum]] of those who oppose us, and break their most wicked [[45:10|weapons|arma]] against us: that, [[45:10|wars|bellis]] being taken away by thy power, we may for ever [[45:11|be still|vacemus]] for thee, [[45:11|and see|et videamus]] that thou art God.

46.title: EXPOSITIO PSALMI QUADRAGESIMI SEXTI : OMNES GENTES, PLAUDITE MANIBUS.
46.title_en: Exposition of the forty-sixth psalm: O clap your hands, all ye nations.

paras.t: Titulus psalmi est : In finem, pro filiis Core, psalmus David : cujus intellectus ex expositione titulorum præcedentium clarus est. Propheta autem in hoc psalmo fideles ad congratulandum Christo ascendenti invitat, et ad laudandum Dominum pro beneficiis ejus, et ait :
paras.en: The title of the psalm is: [[46:1|Unto the end, for the sons of Core|In finem, pro filiis Core]], a psalm of David; its meaning is clear from the exposition of the titles that went before. In this psalm the Prophet invites the faithful to rejoice with Christ as he ascends, and to praise the Lord for his benefits, and he says:

paras.t: Omnes gentes ad fidem conversæ, plaudite manibus : id est, tam cordialiter exsultate, ut ex copia interioris lætitiæ exteriora membra ad Dei honorem ac laudem extendantur, interioremque hilaritatem ostendant, sicut Apostolus Timotheum docens ait : Levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione. Et Jeremias, Leva, inquit, ad Deum manus tuas, et miserebitur tui. Vel sic : Plaudite manibus, id est, bonis operibus Deum laudate et honorate. Hoc enim est optimum genus laudandi Altissimum, actibus virtuosis venerari majestatem ipsius. Propter quod scriptum est : Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ. Jubilate Deo, id est, ad gloriam Dei ineffabiliter eum laudate, in voce exsultationis, id est cum jucundo præconio oris. Jubilus enim est inexpressibile gaudium cordis, quod nec occultari potest in toto, nec exprimi valet ex integro. Vult ergo Propheta, ut tantam Dei laudem concipiat anima nostra, quod eam ore explicare non possit.
paras.en: [[46:2|All ye nations|Omnes gentes]] converted to the faith, [[46:2|O clap your hands|plaudite manibus]]: that is, exult so heartily that, from the abundance of gladness within, your outward members are stretched out to the honour and praise of God and show the joy within, as the Apostle says, teaching Timothy: [[1 Tim 2:8|lifting up pure hands, without anger and contention|Levantes puras manus sine ira et disceptatione]]. And Jeremias says: Lift up thy hands to God, and he will have mercy on thee[[Lam 2:19||]] [there is no margin reference here; the nearest words are Lam 2:19, "lift up thy hands to him", and Lam 3:41, "Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to the Lord"]. Or thus: [[46:2|O clap your hands|Plaudite manibus]], that is, praise and honour God with good works. For this is the best kind of praising the Most High: to venerate his majesty with virtuous acts. For which reason it is written: [[Jas 3:13|Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge, among you? Let him shew, by a good contestation, his work in the meekness of wisdom|Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiæ]]. [[46:2|Shout unto God|Jubilate Deo]], that is, praise him beyond all words to the glory of God, [[46:2|with the voice of joy|in voce exsultationis]], that is, with glad proclamation of the mouth. For jubilation [*jubilus*: a wordless cry of joy] is an inexpressible joy of the heart, which can neither be wholly hidden nor fully expressed. The Prophet wills, then, that our soul conceive so great a praise of God that it cannot unfold it with the mouth.

paras.t: Quoniam Dominus excelsus, id est incomprehensibilis, sublimis, atque immensus ; terribilis, quum sit judex infallibilis, districtus, et justus ; rex magnus super omnem terram : in ditione enim ejus cuncta sunt posita, et omnia elementa ei subjecta sunt. De hac excellentia ad sanctum Job dicitur : Excelsior cœlo est, et quid facies? Profundior inferno, et unde cognosces ? Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari. Si subverterit omnia vel in unum coarctaverit, quis contradicet ei? Et rursus : Columnæ, inquit, cœli contremiscunt et pavent ad nutum ipsius. Et alibi ait sermo divinus : Ecce cœlum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur, montes simul et colles; et quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur. Quam magnus vero et liber ac potens rex sit Deus super omnem terram, ostenditur ubi Dominus ait ad Job : Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ ? Indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam. Quis posuit mensuras ejus ? et quis tendit super eam lineam ? aut super quo bases ejus consolidatæ sunt ?
paras.en: [[46:3|For the Lord is high|Quoniam Dominus excelsus]], that is, incomprehensible, sublime and immeasurable; [[46:3|terrible|terribilis]], since he is a judge who cannot err, strict and just; [[46:3|a great king over all the earth|rex magnus super omnem terram]]: for all things are placed under his dominion, and all the elements are subject to him. Of this excellence it is said to holy Job: [[Job 11:8|He is higher than heaven, and what wilt thou do? he is deeper than hell, and how wilt thou know?|Excelsior cœlo est, et quid facies? Profundior inferno, et unde cognosces]] [[Job 11:9|The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea|Longior terra mensura ejus, et latior mari]]. [[Job 11:10|If he shall overturn all things, or shall press them together, who shall contradict him?|Si subverterit omnia vel in unum coarctaverit, quis contradicet ei?]] And again: [[Job 26:11|The pillars|Columnæ]], he says, [[Job 26:11|of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck|cœli contremiscunt et pavent ad nutum ipsius]]. And elsewhere the divine word says: [[Ecclus 16:18|Behold the heaven, and the heavens of heavens, the deep, and all the earth, and the things that are in them, shall be moved in his sight|Ecce cœlum et cœli cœlorum, abyssus et universa terra, et omnia quæ in eis sunt, in conspectu Dei commovebuntur]], [[Ecclus 16:19|The mountains also, and the hills|montes simul et colles]]; and [[Ecclus 16:19|when God shall look upon them, they shall be shaken with trembling|quum conspexerit illa Deus, tremore concutientur]]. How great, how free and how mighty a king God is over all the earth is shown where the Lord says to Job: [[Job 38:4|Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? tell me if thou hast understanding.|Ubi eras quando ponebam fundamenta terræ ? Indica mihi, si habes intelligentiam]] [[Job 38:5|Who hath laid the measures thereof|Quis posuit mensuras ejus]]? and [[Job 38:5|who hath stretched the line upon it|quis tendit super eam lineam]]? or [[Job 38:6|Upon what are its bases grounded|super quo bases ejus consolidatæ sunt]]?
